IPv6 Toolkit

Inspect any IPv6 address — type, scope, EUI-64 MAC, embedded IPv4, multicast and neighbor discovery — normalize or extract address lists, convert SLAAC and NAT64 addresses, plan ULA / VLAN /64s and ISP prefix delegation with RouterOS config, and build ip6.arpa reverse zones.

Split view

Windows, macOS, iOS and Android give hosts random interface IDs (stable-privacy RFC 7217, temporary RFC 8981), so their SLAAC address can't be predicted from the MAC. Routers (every RouterOS link-local), switches, printers, IoT and many Linux servers still use EUI-64.

NAT64 lets IPv6-only clients reach IPv4 servers: DNS64 answers with the server's IPv4 inside the prefix, and the NAT64 gateway translates. To find a network's prefix, look up ipv4only.arpa AAAA (RFC 7050) and paste the answer here. 464XLAT (RFC 6877) uses the same mapping.

RouterOS script


  

  
How it works: each router gets one aggregate to announce upstream (iBGP / OSPF) holding its delegation pool and, with numbered WAN, its WAN pool. Pools are sized for the subscribers plus headroom, rounded up to a power of two (and to a nibble), so a router can grow without renumbering. RIPE-690 recommends a /56 or /48 per customer, kept stable. RouterOS pools hand prefixes out dynamically, so a subscriber can get a different one after reconnecting — assign fixed prefixes from RADIUS (Delegated-IPv6-Prefix) if they need to stay put.
